text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent camping trip in Minnesota and the pattern of migrating joint pain, did you notice a rash that looked like a bullseye or a tick bite on your body during or shortly after the trip?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on your hands and wrists, combined with arthritis following a tick-endemic camping trip, is highly specific. I will request blood tests to confirm this diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Lyme_serology

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal Lyme serology rules out Lyme disease, so let's look at other possibilities. Have you had any recent exposure to fresh water or soil, or noticed any animal bites, and do you recall having a high fever before the joint pain started?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. Social history: Admits to being sexually active with one female partner who uses a diaphragm for contraception. Recently went on a camping trip to Minnesota.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal Lyme serology and the specific description of painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the hands strongly suggest Sporotrichosis, often caused by gardening or exposure to soil and plant matter. Let me examine your lymph nodes for any signs of lymphangitis or swelling that might indicate the infection is spreading.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies trauma to the wrist, reports a history of knee pain that resolved on its own. No other systemic symptoms mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the acute monoarticular arthritis, fever, and characteristic painful vesiculopustular lesions on the hands, this presentation is classic for disseminated gonococcal infection. I will request a joint aspiration to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Synovial_fluid_analysis
